hypothesis: The rlm.spawn admission cost (~290-342ms p50 recorded by the spawn-latency lane) lives in the supervisor Create route + worker create handler + reply tail; the two big phases from that lane's single-trial daemon-log split (registered->create-done ~168ms, create-done->reply ~171ms) decompose into per-phase costs that are dominated by serialized durability writes (fresh-file + sync_all + rename / append + sync_data) sampled from a TIME-VARYING host storage regime (~0.3ms quiet / ~38-45ms degraded), plus a deterministic ~15-17ms cold first-model-resolve and a 25ms-quantized socket-probe backoff; process exec, worker boot, wire, roster seeding, and kernel provisioning are NOT on the critical path.
approach: MEASUREMENT ONLY, no product change. Inherited the spawn-latency lane's driver/VM contract (same probe design, per-trial-queue mock, warm kernel venv, mock :8890) with a lane-local copy: spawn_admission_probe.py (pidfile single-driver guard, trials-adm/, admission-trace collection; ledger fields extended not replaced). Two evidence arms on the same VM: (A) clean legs on the ARCHIVED baseline binary (pin 7064d039a, sha 994c5563) - cold_warmvenv n=10 + warm_daemon n=8; (B) labeled trace legs on an instrument build at the SAME pin (env-gated PI_ADMISSION_TRACE=1 eprintln, zero default-path change, shas 2bb3c826 then 6f9816eb with finer create-entry probes) - cold n=10 + warm n=8 + fine n=4. ~30 probe points across the supervisor Create route (dispatch, name-assert, launch, spawn, probe loop, connect, auth, create route, post-create persists, spawn-ledger admission record, get_state, roster, family seed), the worker (main, config, Worker::new, serve bind, command dispatch, handle_create internals: fresh-path, lease, rewrite#1, rewrite#2, name entry, settings, core, rlm identity, bind jobs, recovery journal, notify, response write), the registration loop (epoch-1 register, epoch-2 re-register round trips), and the parent worker (spawn entry, model resolve, create start/done, exit). Timestamps: UNIX_EPOCH ns wall clocks, cross-checked per trial against kernel receipts (wall vs perf_counter) and the supervisor RotatingLog epoch lines; raw arrays parsed from trial JSON, no manual transcription. Plus host-regime characterization: a fresh-file+fsync+rename micro-probe (the class the product writes), an O_APPEND+fsync probe, the inherited 4KB repeat-fsync probe, and a two-process concurrent probe - demonstrating the fresh-write class is regime-flipping (0.26ms p50 -> 41ms p50 within minutes, loadavg flat) while the repeat-fsync class stays quiet (0.11ms) - the inherited probe cannot see the class that dominates the product path.
parity_notes: No product code changed in any evidence arm; frozen parity untouched. The instrument is env-gated (PI_ADMISSION_TRACE) with a one-atomic-load disabled path; trace legs are labeled and never mixed with clean legs; trace-vs-clean admission p50s (A-cold 353 vs B-cold 317; A-warm 234 vs B-warm 249) show no systematic instrument overhead (within window variance). Mock provider offline-only; parent/child model prime-inference/mock-1; fixtures deterministic; records carry sha256/counts only.

phase_ledger_notes.durability_phases: descriptor persist#1 (post-exec), child session rewrite#1 (header-only first write), child session rewrite#2 (prefix+state), child name persist_entry (sync_data), child recovery journal (sync_all), supervisor persist#2 (post-create-response), supervisor spawn-ledger append + child display write (admission record) - each samples the host fresh-write regime; per-trial stall counts (ops >= 20ms) run 2-6 per admission and fully explain the bimodal admission distribution (2-3 stalls -> 148-260ms; 4-6 stalls -> 320-400ms)
phase_ledger_notes.deterministic_non_fsync: configure_create_model 15-17ms on EVERY child trial (the cold first model resolve: effective_thinking -> resolve_model on the fresh worker; finer probes bracket all adjacent parsing at ~0); name-assert (O(residents) get_state fan-out) 2.5-3.3ms; fresh get_state route 2.3-2.5ms; Worker::new 2.3ms; core lock block 1.4ms; exec 0.29ms; wire + reply tail ~0.6ms total
phase_ledger_notes.probe_quantization: WORKER_CONNECT_BACKOFF_MS=25 quantizes the socket probe: p50 0.05ms (persist#1's own stall usually delays the probe past the worker's bind at ~2.4ms post-exec) but max 41.7ms when the probe starts before bind (eats the 25ms sleep + executor skew); the constant is a TS-parity port and is NOT a candidate

decision: orchestrator ACCEPTED the ledger and APPROVED the parity-safe candidate: collapse the fresh-path session-file write sequence in the worker create handler (rewrite#1 header-only + rewrite#2 prefix/state + name persist_entry -> ONE rewrite after assembling prefix+state+name in memory; same entries, same order, byte-identical final file, lease timing and failure paths unchanged; expected -2 durability ops per admission: ~-76-90ms admission p50 in the degraded fresh-write regime, ~-1ms in a quiet regime). NOT-candidates confirmed by the orchestrator: spawn-ledger/display durability gating (crash contract by design), probe backoff constant (TS-parity), persist#2 coalescing (disclosed only), the 15-17ms cold resolve (pre-warm would delay bind -> probe eats it, net zero). Candidate requirements from the orchestrator: differential oracle (assembled single write == sequential writes' final bytes, ts-masked, incl. crash-recovery replay classes), crash-window tests for the changed shape, paired ABBA in BOTH storage regimes with regime-labeled claims, frozen-parity oracles (admission wire, JSONL content, family seed) every arm.
